title.value: Memory Efficient Neural Processes via Constant Memory Attention Block
title.justification: The title 'Memory Efficient Neural Processes via Constant Memory Attention Block' is clearly stated at the beginning of the paper and encapsulates the primary focus of the research, which is on developing memory-efficient neural processes through a novel attention mechanism.
title.quote: Memory Efficient Neural Processes via Constant Memory Attention Block

extractions.description: The paper introduces a memory-efficient variant of Neural Processes called Constant Memory Attentive Neural Processes (CMANPs). The focus is on improving computational efficiency and reducing memory usage, especially in low-resource settings such as IoT devices and mobile robots. The paper proposes an efficient update operation for Cross Attention that enables CMANPs to achieve state-of-the-art results with significantly reduced memory requirements compared to previous methods.

climate_change_is_central.justification: While the paper focuses on improving the memory efficiency of neural processes, it does not directly address Climate Change or related environmental issues as its central theme. The applications mentioned are more general in the context of machine learning and computational efficiency.
climate_change_is_central.quote: In this paper, we improve the memory efficiency of Neural Processes, a family of deep learning models for uncertainty estimation. In order to deploy deep learning models to real-world settings, it is imperative that the models be memory efficient whilst simultaneously being able to capture their predictive uncertainty; incorrect or overconfident predictions can have dire consequences in mission- or safety-critical settings (Tambon et al., 2022).

primary_category.justification: The paper does not directly pertain to Climate Change or its associated categories. It primarily deals with neural process efficiencies which may indirectly benefit sustainable technologies, but Climate Change is not the main focus.
primary_category.quote: In this paper, we improve the memory efficiency of Neural Processes, a family of deep learning models for uncertainty estimation.

secondary_categories.justification: Given that Climate Change is not central to the paper, there are no secondary categories related to Climate Change.
secondary_categories.quote: The design of memory-efficient models is crucial for settings with a limited energy supply.

primary_sub_category.justification: There is no specific sub-category within Climate Change that this paper aligns with, since its focus is on computational efficiency of neural processes.
primary_sub_category.quote: The paper proposes Constant Memory Attentive Neural Processes (CMANPs), a new memory-efficient NP variant.

new_primary_category.justification: The paper's central focus is on optimizing memory usage and computational efficiency in neural processes, which is an area not explicitly covered in existing Climate Change categories, warranting a new classification.
new_primary_category.quote: To do so, we propose Constant Memory Attentive Neural Processes (CMANPs), an NP variant that only requires constant memory.

new_primary_sub_category.value: Efficient Deep Learning Models for Low-Resource Settings
new_primary_sub_category.justification: The focus on developing memory-efficient models, particularly for deployment in low-resource and energy-constrained environments, suggests a specialized sub-category of making deep learning models adaptable to such settings.
new_primary_sub_category.quote: With the growing popularity of low-memory/compute domains (e.g., IoT devices and mobile phones), deployed models in these low-resource settings must be memory efficient.
